chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who is not concerned with the affairs of the Muslims is not a Muslim.

key_terms.فَلَيْسَ بِمُسْلِمٍ: so he is not a Muslim
key_terms.يَهْتَمَّ: to be concerned / to take interest

ai.seo_question: What is the sign of a true Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), establishing that *ihtimam* (active concern) is not merely a recommended virtue but a constitutive element of Islamic identity. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *al-amr bi-l-ma'ruf wa al-nahy 'an al-munkar* (commanding good and forbidding evil) as a communal obligation, linking individual piety directly to social responsibility and mutual care within the Ummah.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad Bin Al Qasim Al Hashimy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who is not concerned with the affairs of the Muslims, so he is not a Muslim’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Muhammad al-Qasim al-Hashimi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever does not feel any concern about the affairs of Muslims is not a Muslim any longer.”
